turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same n-i-p (regular) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
I'll analyze the training data systematically, then evaluate each candidate against the patterns learned.

## Step 1: Extract Key Patterns from Training Data

### Substrate
- SLG | FTO and SLG | ITO dominate high-efficiency devices
- FTO slightly more common in top performers

### ETL patterns (high-efficiency correlates):
- **TiO2-c | SnO2-np** → 20.85% (highest!)
- **TiO2-c | PCBM-60** → 19.35%, 14.25%, 16.91% (with C60-ETA)
- **TiO2-c | BaSnO3-np** → 18.9%
- **SnO2-c | PCBM-60** → 17.28%, 18.0%
- **TiO2-c | C60** → 17.2%, 12.705%
- **TiO2-c** (plain) → spans wide range, but with good HTL can reach 18-19%
- **SnO2-c** → 14.72%, 16.085%, 16.9%
- **ZnO-np | SnO2-np** → 17.3%
- **TiO2-c | SnO2** → 17.47%
- **TiO2-c | Graphene-QDs** → 17.405%
- **TiO2-c | Au@TiO2-np; TiO2-mp** → 17.325%

### HTL patterns:
- **Spiro-MeOTAD** is by far the most common high-efficiency HTL
- **PTAA** → excellent: 18.19% (SnO2-np/PTAA/Ag), 18.9%, 15.3%, 15.46%, 16.5%
- **PCDTBT1** → 19.35%
- **PbS-QDs | Spiro-MeOTAD** → 18.63%
- **IEICO-4F | Spiro-MeOTAD** → 18.965%
- **PHPT-py** → 18.73%
- Novel organic HTMs with Spiro-MeOTAD tend to be high

### Back contact:
- **Au** → most common in high-efficiency
- **Ag** → also high efficiency
- **MoO3 | Au** → 19.35%
- **MoO3 | Ag** → good

### Deposition:
- **Spin-coating** (single or multiple steps) dominates high efficiency
- **Spin-coating >> Spin-coating** very common in top devices
- **CBD** additions sometimes help

## Step 2: Evaluate Top Candidates

Let me focus on candidates with the most promising combinations:

**c005**: SLG|ITO, TiO2-c|PCBM-60, PCDTBT8, MoO3|Au, Spin-coating>>Spin-coating
- Nearly identical to the 19.35% training entry (TiO2-c|PCBM-60, PCDTBT1, MoO3|Au). PCDTBT8 is a variant of PCDTBT1. This is the closest analog to the highest-efficiency non-SnO2 device. Very strong candidate.

**c017**: SLG|ITO, C60;PhIm|C60, TaTM|F6-TCNNQ;TaTm, Ag, Co-evaporation
- Nearly identical to training entry: C60;Phlm|C60, TaTm|F6-TCNNQ;TaTm, Au, Co-evaporation → 17.9%. Ag vs Au back contact is minor. Strong candidate.

**c068**: SLG|ITO, SnO2-np|TiO2-np, PTAA, Au|MoO3, Spin-coating
- SnO2-np ETL with PTAA HTL. Training shows SnO2-np/PTAA/Ag → 18.19%. Bilayer ETL (SnO2-np|TiO2-np) adds electron selectivity. PTAA is excellent HTL. Au|MoO3 is a good ohmic contact. Very strong.

**c064**: SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|SnO2-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- TiO2-c|SnO2-np ETL is the same as the 20.85% training entry! HTL is Spiro-MeOTAD (vs Spiro-MeOTAD in that entry too). The 20.85% entry used Ag; here Au. This is essentially the champion architecture with Au instead of Ag — should be very high.

**c025**: SLG|FTO, SnO2-c|TiO2-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, Ag, Spin-coating>>CBD
- SnO2-c|TiO2-np bilayer ETL. Training: SnO2-c|TiO2-c → 16.54%, SnO2-c|PCBM-60 → 17.28-18.0%. Bilayer oxide ETL with Spiro-MeOTAD and Ag is solid. Good but not top-5 lock.

**c073**: SLG|ITO-HMDS Scaffold, TiO2-c|C60, PTAA, Ag, Spin-coating
- TiO2-c|C60 ETL (training: 17.2% with Spiro-MeOTAD/Ag) + PTAA (better than Spiro). Training: TiO2-c|C60/PTAA/Ag → 16.5%. The HMDS scaffold on ITO improves wettability/morphology. Competitive.

**c045**: SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-nanofibers, PTAA, Au, Spin-coating
- TiO2-c|TiO2-nanofibers ETL (training: 12.06% with Spiro-MeOTAD/Au). PTAA instead of Spiro-MeOTAD should boost significantly. PTAA is known to give ~3-4% absolute improvement over Spiro in many architectures. Could reach ~15-17%.

**c021**: PEN|ITO, SnO2-np|CPTA, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- CPTA is a self-assembled monolayer passivator on SnO2. Training: PEN|ITO/SnO2-np/Spiro-MeOTAD/Ag → 11.87%. CPTA passivation of SnO2 interface is known to boost PCE. Could reach ~14-16%.

**c080**: SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|MPMIC60, Spiro-MeOTAD, Ag, Spin-coating
- MPMIC60 is a fullerene derivative ETL interlayer. Similar to TiO2-c|PCBM-60 (14.25%) or TiO2-c|C60 (17.2%). Reasonable but uncertain.

**c031**: SLG|FTO, SnO2-c|SnO2-mp|TiO2-c, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- Triple ETL stack. SnO2-c|TiO2-c → 16.54% in training. Adding SnO2-mp could help or hurt (more interfaces). Moderate.

**c013**: SLG|FTO, TiO2-c, P(VDF-TrFE)|Spiro-MeOTAD, MoO3|Ag, Spin-coating
- Ferroelectric interlayer P(VDF-TrFE) under Spiro. Training: IEICO-4F|Spiro-MeOTAD → 18.965%, PbS-QDs|Spiro-MeOTAD → 18.63%. Ferroelectric interlayers can enhance built-in field. Potentially high.

**c015**: SLG|ITO, C60;C70, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- Mixed fullerene ETL. Training: C60/Spiro-MeOTAD/MoO3|Ag → 15.05%, C60/Spiro-MeOTAD/Au → 12.11%. C60+C70 mix may improve morphology. Moderate ~14-16%.

**c055**: SLG|ITO, TiO2-c, PTB7, Au, Spin-coating
- PTB7 as HTL. Training: TiO2-c|TiO2-mp/PTB7/Ag → 12.65%. Plain TiO2-c with PTB7 and Au. Moderate.

**c005 deep analysis**: The training entry "TiO2-c|PCBM-60, PCDTBT1, MoO3|Au" = 19.35%. PCDTBT8 is a structural variant. The ETL (TiO2-c|PCBM-60) provides excellent electron extraction, PCBM passivates TiO2 surface traps. PCDTBT-family HTMs have deep HOMO (~5.5 eV) matching MAPbI3 VBM well. MoO3|Au ohmic contact. This is the strongest analog to a near-champion device.

**c064 deep analysis**: TiO2-c|SnO2-np is the exact ETL of the 20.85% champion. SnO2 has better band alignment with MAPbI3 (CBM ~4.0 eV vs TiO2 ~4.2 eV, but SnO2 ~4.5 eV gives stronger driving force), lower trap density, higher electron mobility. The bilayer TiO2-c|SnO2-np combines TiO2-c as hole-blocking compact layer with SnO2-np for superior electron extraction. Spiro-MeOTAD/Au is the standard high-performance HTL/contact. Au vs Ag: Au gives better stability and slightly better work function match. This should be very close to 20.85%.

**c068 deep analysis**: SnO2-np|TiO2-np bilayer ETL — both are n-type oxides. SnO2 (higher electron affinity) next to ITO, TiO2-np on perovskite side. PTAA is arguably the best HTL for MAPbI3 (HOMO ~5.2 eV, good match). Au|MoO3 — MoO3 as hole injection layer before Au is excellent. ITO substrate is standard. This combination is very strong.

**c017 deep analysis**: The co-evaporation of C60;PhIm|C60 ETL with TaTm|F6-TCNNQ;TaTm HTL (doped transport layers) is a fully evaporated architecture. Training analog: 17.9%. Ag vs Au back contact — minor difference. Should be ~17-18%.

## Step 3: Ranking

1. **c064** — TiO2-c|SnO2-np ETL (exact match to 20.85% champion ETL) + Spiro-MeOTAD/Au. Highest expected PCE.

2. **c005** — TiO2-c|PCBM-60 + PCDTBT8 (analog of PCDTBT1) + MoO3|Au. Near-analog to 19.35% device.

3. **c068** — SnO2-np|TiO2-np + PTAA + Au|MoO3. SnO2-based ETL + best-in-class HTL. ~18-19% expected.

4. **c017** — Fully evaporated doped transport layers, analog to 17.9% training entry.

5. **c013** — TiO2-c + P(VDF-TrFE)|Spiro-MeOTAD + MoO3|Ag. Ferroelectric interlayer enhances Voc; training shows composite HTLs (IEICO-4F|Spiro → 18.97%, PbS-QDs|Spiro → 18.63%) can exceed plain Spiro significantly.

Alternatively c073 (TiO2-c|C60/PTAA/Ag on ITO-HMDS) could edge out c013, but the HMDS scaffold is unusual and the training analog (TiO2-c|C60/PTAA/Ag) = 16.5% without scaffold enhancement.

**Final: c064, c005, c068, c017, c013**
